texts.preamble: M/S.Rain Dropps R.O. Water Private Ltd vs The Commissioner on 15 November, 2022 Author: N. Sathish Kumar Bench: N. Sathish Kumar W.P.No.40642 of In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 15.11.2022 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice N. Sathish Kumar W.P.No.40642 of 2016 and W.M.P.No.34657 of 2016 M/s.Rain Dropps R.O. Water Private Ltd
texts.facts: ORDER This petition has been filed challenging the order of the second respondent dated 11.11.2016 issued under R.No.498/2016/A1 directing the petitioner company to close and stop all the activities forthwith including manufacture or process, packing, store, distribution, sale or whatsoever by any means in the name of the petitioner company until further orders. 2. This writ petition has been filed challenging the impugned order mainly on the grounds that it violates principle of natural justice and the compliance report of the petitioner has not been considered and completely ignored. The impugned order violates Section 32 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and affects the rights of the petitioner. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3. It is the case of the petitioner that the third respondent viz., the Food Safety Officer inspected the petitioner company unit on 16.07.2016 and drawn the samples of water for the purpose of testing i.e., so as to test whether the water collected satisfy the norms of the FSSAI standards. Further, the Food Analyst gave a report stating that the samples are found to be unsafe for human consumption and thereafter, the prosecution also launched a case against the petitioner company.
texts.arguments: It is the grievance of the petitioner that the prosecution has been launched only on the basis of the report given by the Food Analyst. Hence, seeks to allow this writ petition. 4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the present impugned order has been passed without following due procedure as contemplated in the eye of law, whereas, the learned Government Advocate submitted that the water samples collected from the petitioner company from the year 2017 to till date and the report issued by the Food Analyst would indicate that the samples are unsafe for human consumption. He has also filed an additional typed-set of papers containing copy of the report of the food analyst dated 10.11.2022, which would indicate that the water is unsafe for the human consumption. He further submitted that petitioner has to close the business, if at https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis all the petitioner company wants to continue the operation of the business, they should set right all the mistakes within a period of three months. After the period of three months, the petitioner ought to allow the respondents officials to draw the samples of the petitioner company and if the samples come within the parameters of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the petitioner may start operation. Consenting, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner will close the business and they will set right all the defects pointed out by the respondent officials and start their projects after three months i.e., only after examination by the Food Analyst and if found that the water is safe for human consumption. 6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Advocate and perused the materials placed on record.
texts.petitioner_arguments: It is the grievance of the petitioner that the prosecution has been launched only on the basis of the report given by the Food Analyst. He has also filed an additional typed-set of papers containing copy of the report of the food analyst dated 10.11.2022, which would indicate that the water is unsafe for the human consumption. He further submitted that petitioner has to close the business, if at https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis all the petitioner company wants to continue the operation of the business, they should set right all the mistakes within a period of three months. After the period of three months, the petitioner ought to allow the respondents officials to draw the samples of the petitioner company and if the samples come within the parameters of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the petitioner may start operation. Consenting, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner will close the business and they will set right all the defects pointed out by the respondent officials and start their projects after three months i.e., only after examination by the Food Analyst and if found that the water is safe for human consumption. 6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Advocate and perused the materials placed on record.
